tip: के साथ (ke saath) = physically 'with': परिवार के साथ (parivaar ke saath = with his family). Don't mix it up with के पास (ke paas), which means 'near' or 'have'.
अपने आप (apne aap) = by oneself: Kavita finished सारा काम (saara kaam = all the work) with no help. For things, the same phrase means 'on its own'.
मनवा ही ली (manva hi li) – मानना (maanna = accept) plus -वा means getting OTHERS to accept: Vikas didn't just state अपनी बात (apni baat = his point), he made them agree.
ना (na) tacked onto a command doesn't negate – it softens it into a plea: मत जाओ ना (mat jao na) = 'please don't go'.
Hindi often drops है (hai) after a negative: पसंद नहीं (pasand nahin) alone means 'doesn't like it' – no 'is' needed at the end.
जाना (jaana = go) glued onto a verb marks completion: रुक जाओ (ruk jao) = come to a full stop. Plain रुको (ruko) is just 'stop'.
'Not as...as' is a matched pair in Hindi: उतना साफ़ नहीं जितना (utna saaf nahin jitna) = literally 'not that-much clean, as-much-as'. Two words where English repeats 'as'.
Hindi says 'anywhere + not' where English says 'nowhere': कहीं भी शांति नहीं मिलती (kahin bhi shanti nahin milti) = literally 'anywhere peace is not found'.
न...न (na...na) means 'neither...nor' – a third negator besides नहीं (nahin) and मत (mat): न प्रिया आई, न कोई संदेश (na Priya aayi, na koi sandesh).
Skills 'come' to you in Hindi: तैरना आता ही नहीं (tairna aata hi nahin) = literally 'swimming just doesn't come (to me)' = I can't swim. आना (aana = to come) covers know-how.
Cars 'stand' in Hindi: खड़ी की (khari ki) = parked, literally 'made it stand'. गाड़ी खड़ी करना (gaadi khari karna) = to park a car.
'Not yet' = अभी तक...नहीं (abhi tak...nahin), literally 'until now not': मैंने अभी तक वह फ़िल्म नहीं देखी (maine abhi tak vah film nahin dekhi) = I haven't seen that film yet.
You 'drink' a cigarette in Hindi: सिगरेट मत पियो (cigarette mat piyo) = don't smoke, literally 'don't drink a cigarette'. पीना (peena) covers smoking too.
A command built on the infinitive is for later or gentler: देर मत करना (der mat karna) = 'don't be late (when the time comes)'. मत करो (mat karo) orders it right now.
English fills the bottle – Hindi flips it: बोतल में ठंडा पानी भरा है (botal mein thanda paani bhara hai = in the bottle cold water is filled). The container gets में (mein), the water is the subject.
Hindi position words come after their word, not before: यहाँ से (yahaan se = here from) = from here. Every from, on, in trails its word – mez par, subah se.
For breakfast is नाश्ते में (naashte mein = in breakfast), not ke liye. Meals take में (mein): you make things in breakfast, in lunch.
No word for to with going: हवाई अड्डा कैसे जाएँ (hawai adda kaise jaaen = how to go airport). Destinations of jaana usually take nothing – ghar jao, school jao.
Hindi says where things are placed, not that they exist: फ्रिज में दूध रखा है (fridge mein doodh rakha hai = milk is kept in the fridge) is the everyday way to say there is milk.
तक (tak) means both until and by: शाम तक (shaam tak) here is by evening, a deadline; shaam tak kaam kiya would be until evening. Context picks the reading.
Trains walk in Hindi: चलती है (chalti hai = moves) is how the train departs from the platform. चलना (chalna) covers vehicles and machines – a working watch chalti hai too.
English lumps all uncles together – Hindi is precise: फूफाजी (phoophaji) is specifically your father's sister's husband. The जी (ji) on the end adds respect.
Doubling stretches a word: दूर-दूर तक (door-door tak = up to far-far) = far and wide. Hindi repeats words for spread – kabhi-kabhi is sometimes, dheere-dheere is slowly.
Hindi meets from people: रूपा से मिलिए (Roopa se miliye = meet Roopa). To meet someone, मिलना (milna) takes से (se), never a plain object like English meet.
से (se) doubles as by for any means: बस से (bus se) = by bus. Transport, payment, tools all take से – card se, haath se (by hand).
की (ki) agrees with the thing owned, not the owner: सुषमा की किताब (Sushma ki kitaab) uses feminine की because kitaab is feminine – Sushma's own gender is irrelevant.
Hindi has no verb for to have – people just exist in your space: मेरे ऑफिस में बहुत अच्छे साथी हैं (mere office mein bahut achche saathi hain = in my office are very good colleagues).
से (se) also marks causes: दर्द होने से (dard hone se = from pain happening) = because of the pain. Verb + hone se is the everyday due to.
Phones close in Hindi: फ़ोन बंद हो गया (phone band ho gaya = the phone became closed) = it died or switched off. बंद (band) covers closed and off – shops, lights, phones.
पर (par) means on, but it is also Hindi's at: बस स्टॉप पर (bus stop par) = at the bus stop. There is no separate word – station par, ghar par.
